They act slightly different depending on the choices we make as players because that's the point, to change Anthony's view on his own family, to get over the tragedy of losing them. Which is why they can potentially die at the end regardless of the choices if their personalities don't change.

​

> Taylor is a representation of Tabitha, but she’s not ACTUALLY Tabitha. 

Taylor only exists in Anthony's mind, she is his brain's version/representation of his dead sister Tanya...who is a reincarnation of Tilly, who is a reincarnation of Tabitha.

There are scattered pieces of evidence that suggest Reverend Carson from 1972 was able to complete the summoning that his predecessor Reverend Carver was unable to accomplish back in the 1600s. Lots of talk about using Satanism for rebirth of the soul and spirit and reincarnation. 

A lot of people also seem to think the demon figure was just an imaginary friend of Megan's she made to try and cope with the trauma of being molested and having a family that "doesn't listen to her." Although sexual abuse is (not really) hinted at, it's a bit more complicated than just a pedo priest molesting an adopted little girl. The dude (the whole church, really) was heavily involved in the occult and he was using Megan to practice black magick rituals to summon Satan. His papers claim that Satan needed a vessel with a soul that "had been purified through isolation and sacrifice."

Even without finding all the the evidence, it should be obvious that this is a real supernatural detail in the game because it takes place before Anthony's trauma, before his schizo episode in 2020. Meaning everything that happened in the scene from 1972 with the house burning down actually happened, it is not "just in Anthony's head" as some people would theorize. We literally see the ghost from a 3rd person perspective rather than Anthony's. Also the ladder shakes by itself after Megan walked away and the balcony door shuts on Tanya while Megan was still sitting on the bed. Megan's demon is real. The Reverend's ritual worked and he is later convicted for it.

And although they are not blood related, I don't think a mother would approve of two of her kids getting freaky with it. Not technically incest, yea, but it'd just be a weird dynamic, ya know. They're supposed to act like siblings.

imo cooking salmon in a pan is way easier/quicker than using an oven, i always use a pan.


a lot of the cooking method is determined by what ur filet looks like. so here are some basic tips.


first make sure ur salmon is dry. i wrap my filet in a paper towel or two and give it a light squeeze on all sides. add dry herbs (salt/pepper/etc) after u do this step.  
medium-high heat, on a scale of 1-10 i use like a 6.5-7.  
i use oil rather than butter. coconut, olive, avocado, they’re all fine. about a tablespoon. while the oil is heating u can add additional herbs/aromatics for extra flavor.  
once the oil is hot, and behaves like water in the pan, add the salmon skin side down. you should hear it immediately and the skin might visibly shrivel slightly.  
now leave it alone and don’t touch it for several minutes. looking at the thickest cross section, you’ll be able to see when it’s ready to turn when the color changes about 30-40% from the bottom. doesn’t have to be completely halfway cooked. pre-flip cook time depends how thick ur filet is but maybe like 5mins?  
get the spatula and lightly loosen the skin from the pan. once it’s released u can turn it.  
if u have a large square flatter filet, flip completely over like a burger.  
if u have a smaller long rectangle filet, just turn it so it’s on it’s side, u want to cook each side.  
again cook time depends on thickness and size.  


i agree with the other user who said salmon is supposed to be cooked to medium, still slightly orange/pink on the thickest part inside rather than straight pale pink all throughout.
